To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a closed expression for repeated derivatives of the inverse of the mass matrix for multibody systems, which rests on the factorized form of the inverse mass matrices, and that we extended this result for the mass matrices of multibody systems with kinematic loops.

1) the inverse mass matrix of open kinematic chains can be factorized in terms of a block-diagonal matrix; 2) the inverse mass matrices of mechanisms with kinematics loops can be factorized as well, but the factorization includes the inverse of the kinematic Jacobian matrix; and 3) the partial derivatives of the mass and inverse mass matrices are given in terms derivatives of the diagonal matrices.
we have developed a closed expression for repeated derivatives of the inverse of a symmetric positive definite matrix in terms of the inverse itself and its derivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of closed expressions for the partial derivatives of the mass and inverse mass matrix of multibody systems with kinematic loops.
the development of closed expressions for the partial derivatives of the mass matrix of multibody systems.
the development of closed expressions for the partial derivatives of the mass matrices of multibody systems with kinematic loops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in contrast to the mass matrix itself, the inverse mass matrix of open kinematic chains can be factorized in terms of configuration dependent block-diagonal matrices.
the partial derivatives of the mass matrix of a mechanism with kinematic loops are nonvanishing if and only if the partial derivatives of a single diagonal block are nonvanishing.
the partial derivatives of the mass matrix of a multibody system are given in closed form by the partial derivatives of a single block of the block-diagonal factorization of the mass matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inverse of the mass matrix of a mechanism with kinematic loops has a factorization in terms of the inverse of a block diagonal mass matrix.
the factorization of a matrix is a useful tool for the derivation of closed expressions for partial derivatives of this matrix.

we have developed a new method for the computation of partial derivatives of the mass matrix and of the inverse mass matrices of multibody systems, which is applicable to open and closed kinematic chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
partial derivatives of the mass matrix of a multibody system are nontrivial only for a single diagonal block of its factorized form.

partial derivatives of the mass matrix of multibody systems can be computed by evaluating the derivatives of a single block of a block-diagonal matrix that is independent of the number of degrees of freedom of the system.
the partial derivatives of the mass matrix are given as a function of the partial derivatives of a single block of the mass matrix.
